misconceptions.description: Selecting a software case because it has the most features, equating feature count with instructional value.
misconceptions.trigger: team justifies a tool by how many features it offers
misconceptions.feedback: Select for fit, not feature count. Tie one specific affordance to the learning goal; unused features add complexity, not value.

misconceptions.description: Starting from a tool's appealing features and inventing a learning goal to fit them, reversing the design logic.
misconceptions.trigger: team lists tool features first and derives the goal afterward
misconceptions.feedback: Lead with the learning goal and audience, then choose a tool whose affordances serve that goal. Avoid solutions in search of a problem.

misconceptions.description: Choosing a software case without weighing time, cost, and learner-access constraints when goal fit is comparable.
misconceptions.trigger: team picks a tool without any constraint analysis
misconceptions.feedback: When affordance fit is comparable, justify the choice with constraints: setup time, cost, and learner access. Record the tradeoff.
